<PubmedArticle><MedlineCitation Status="MEDLINE" Owner="NLM" IndexingMethod="Manual"><PMID Version="1">28192854</PMID><DateCompleted><Year>2017</Year><Month>09</Month><Day>11</Day></DateCompleted><DateRevised><Year>2018</Year><Month>11</Month><Day>13</Day></DateRevised><Article PubModel="Print-Electronic"><Journal><ISSN IssnType="Electronic">1097-4598</ISSN><JournalIssue CitedMedium="Internet"><Volume>56</Volume><Issue>3</Issue><PubDate><Year>2017</Year><Month>Sep</Month></PubDate></JournalIssue><Title>Muscle &amp; nerve</Title><ISOAbbreviation>Muscle Nerve</ISOAbbreviation></Journal><ArticleTitle>Ingestion of transient receptor potential channel agonists attenuates exercise-induced muscle cramps.</ArticleTitle><Pagination><StartPage>379</StartPage><EndPage>385</EndPage><MedlinePgn>379-385</MedlinePgn></Pagination><ELocationID EIdType="doi" ValidYN="Y">10.1002/mus.25611</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText Label="INTRODUCTION">Exercise-associated muscle cramping (EAMC) is a poorly understood problem that is neuromuscular in origin. Ingestion of transient receptor potential (TRP) channel agonists has been efficacious in attenuating electrically induced muscle cramps. This study examines the effect of TRP agonist ingestion on voluntarily induced EAMC and motor function.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="METHODS">Study 1: Thirty-nine participants completed 2 trials after ingesting TRP agonist-containing active treatment (A), or vehicle (V) control. Cramping in the triceps surae muscle was induced via voluntary isometric contraction. Study 2: After ingesting A or V, 31 participants performed kinematic and psychomotor tests of manual dexterity.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="RESULTS">A increased precramp contraction duration (A, 36.9 &#xb1; 4.1 s; V, 27.8 &#xb1; 3.1 s), decreased cramp EMG area under the curve (A, 37.3 &#xb1; 7.7 %EMG<sub>max</sub> &#xb7;s; V, 77.2 &#xb1; 17.7 %EMG<sub>max</sub> &#xb7;s), increased contraction force to produce the cramp (A, 13.8 &#xb1; 1.8 kg; V, 9.9 &#xb1; 1.6 kg), and decreased postcramp soreness (A, 4.1 &#xb1; 0.3 arbitrary units (a.u.); V, 4.7 &#xb1; 0.3 a.u.). Kinematic and psychomotor tests were not affected.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="DISCUSSION">TRP agonist ingestion attenuated EAMC characteristics without affecting motor function. Muscle Nerve 56: 379-385, 2017.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>&#xa9; 2017 Wiley Periodicals, Inc.</CopyrightInformation></Abstract><AuthorList CompleteYN="Y"><Author
